領.meaning: A bossy <part>rubber duck</part> paddles to the middle of the bath and starts shouting <part>orders</part> at the soap, the sponge and your toes. Everything inside the tub's rim must obey it; past the rim, nobody listens. That bath is its <kanji>jurisdiction</kanji>.
領.on: Soon it claims the whole little <sound>ryo</sound>kan inn around the bath, and the guests must bow as it floats by.
領.kun: Rebels get an <sound>e</sound>gg cracked on their head and a wet <sound>ree</sound>d stuffed down their collar.

農.meaning: A giant <part>clam</part> lies in a muddy field, opening and snapping its shell to plough the furrows, while a farmer hums a <part>melody</part> to keep it in rhythm. When the song speeds up, the clam digs faster. That's modern <kanji>agriculture</kanji>.
農.on: A garden <sound>gno</sound>me rides on top of the shell, scattering seeds from its pointy hat.

栄.meaning: A little <part>tree</part> sleeps under a <part>blanket</part> all winter. On the first warm night, <part>fireworks</part> burst right above it, and by morning it has shot up, thick with leaves, fruit and birdsong. Woken up properly, it starts to <kanji>flourish</kanji>.
栄.on: Its first crop is one golden <sound>a</sound>corn, which bounces off the blanket and rolls away.
栄.kun: A <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>ca</sound>rp leap out of the pond below to nibble at its fruit.

占.meaning: A fortune-teller turns on a <part>faucet</part> above a customer's open <part>mouth</part> and listens to how the water gurgles in the throat. Three gargles mean rain, one splutter means love. That's her way of <kanji>divining</kanji>.
占.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try on guard at her door spits out his gargle and asks for a reading too.
占.kun: Then a <sound>shee</sound>p barges in, drops a <sound>me</sound>lon on the table and takes over her chair: occupied.

規.meaning: A fussy <part>husband</part> sets up a <part>camera</part> at the front door and photographs every visitor next to a painted height chart. Too short, too muddy, too loud: turned away. Only guests who meet his <kanji>standard</kanji> get in.
規.on: Those who pass are handed a brass <sound>key</sound> on a ribbon, and must give it back at midnight.

周.meaning: A racing snail carries a <part>good luck</part> charm in a little wire <part>frame</part> strapped to its shell. Round and round the garden path it goes, charm jingling, until it's back where it started. One full <kanji>circuit</kanji> takes it all afternoon.
周.on: At the finish line the snail is handed its trophy: one tiny golden <sound>shoe</sound>.
周.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' wails a baby snail, dizzy from watching it go round and round.

辺.meaning: A rusty <part>sword</part> lies across a skateboard <part>ramp</part> at the edge of town, and every skater who jumps it lands somewhere different: the bakery roof, the duck pond, the bus stop. By sunset they've been flung onto every street nearby. It's the fastest tour of the <kanji>environs</kanji>.
辺.on: A <sound>hen</sound> in a peaked cap sells tickets at the top of the ramp, clucking out where each jump will land.
辺.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, a <sound>ta</sound>co stand!' cries one skater, landing right beside one just across the road.

働.meaning: Every morning a <part>coat hook</part> sprouts little legs, hops off the wall and begins to <part>move</part> the whole house's laundry from basket to line and back again. No breaks, no pay, just one bent arm and wet socks. It never stops its <kanji>work</kanji>.
働.on: At lunch it kneads a lump of bread <sound>dough</sound> with its one bent arm.
働.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' it laughs, tossing a <sound>ta</sound>co to the cat, then cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!' as the last sock goes up.

七.meaning: A sleepy cat stretches <part>one</part> long paw straight across the rug, and its tail flops down through it in a <part>zigzag</part>. Seen from the ceiling, it looks like a number crossed out. The cat has <kanji>seven</kanji> more naps planned today.
七.on: In every nap it dreams of a <sound>shee</sound>p bringing it a plate of <sound>chee</sound>se.
七.kun: Between naps it nibbles a <sound>na</sound>an, then another <sound>na</sound>an, and goes back to sleep.

疑.meaning: A detective finds a <part>spoon</part>, a <part>dart</part> and a cold <part>pizza wedge</part> stuffed inside a <part>giant boot</part> at the crime scene. The butler swears he's never seen any of them. The detective raises one eyebrow, full of <kanji>doubt</kanji>.
疑.on: In the boot's heel she spots a tiny <sound>gear</sound>, still ticking, and trusts him even less.
疑.kun: She sniffs the boot: a hint of <sound>u</sound>don, a <sound>ta</sound>co, and a lot of <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

基.meaning: Deep in the <part>soil</part>, a mole builds his first tiny <part>bookshelf</part>, and the very first book he shelves is 'How to Dig'. Poetry and maths can wait. Before anything else, a mole has to learn the <kanji>fundamentals</kanji>.
基.on: He locks the bookshelf with a little brass <sound>key</sound> so the worms can't borrow it.
基.kun: The <sound>mo</sound>le props the shelf up on a stubby <sound>to</sound>tem pole, the base of everything.

締.meaning: The <part>emperor</part> has eaten too many dumplings and his robe won't close. Six servants wind <part>thread</part> round and round his belly, leaning back with all their weight, until the buttons stop popping. Every morning they have to <kanji>tighten</kanji> it a little more.
締.on: When the thread runs out, they finish the job with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
締.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p in the corner bleats for its <sound>Ma</sound> as the palace doors slam shut.

互.meaning: <part>Two</part> neighbours own a single clothes <part>iron</part> and pass it back and forth over the fence: today you press my shirts, tomorrow I press yours. Neither has bought one in twenty years. Everything between them is done <kanji>mutually</kanji>.
互.on: Whoever's turn it is wears swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles against the steam.
互.kun: One irons out the other's <sound>ta</sound>co stain; the other returns the favour with a <sound>ga</sound>rlic one.

仮.meaning: A hotel lobby boasts a gleaming <part>coat hook</part> under a sign: '<part>anti</part>-theft, guaranteed'. You hang up your coat, and the whole hook flops over: it's painted cardboard. The guarantee is a <kanji>sham</kanji>.
仮.on: Even the <sound>ca</sound>rp in the lobby pond is cardboard, propped up on a stick.
仮.kun: 'Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm,' says the manager, 'it's just for now,' and props a cardboard <sound>ree</sound>f in the pool.

担.meaning: At <part>daybreak</part> a tiny sailor hauls the ship's <part>anchor</part> out of the sea, heaves it onto his back and trudges inland, sweating. Nobody asked him to; he just thinks someone should carry it. He spends all day <kanji>shouldering</kanji> it.
担.on: His route takes him through a long dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, the anchor scraping sparks off the roof.
担.kun: For lunch he balances a plate of chicken <sound>katsu</sound> on top of the anchor.

評.meaning: A pancake judge stands on a chair and gives a long <part>speech</part> about every entry. Fluffy ones get a cheer, but any pancake <part>flat</part> as paper gets a frown and a low score. It's her job to <kanji>evaluate</kanji> them.
評.on: She taps one tall <sound>hee</sound>l as each plate comes up, and bops the flattest ones with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo.

順.meaning: A line of <part>rubber duck</part> toys floats down the <part>river</part>, nose to tail. When the front duck squeaks, all the rest turn left at once; two squeaks, and they spin. Not one ever swims its own way. They just <kanji>obey</kanji>.
順.on: They squeeze past a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush on the bank, one by one, never out of turn.

態.meaning: A bear with every <part>ability</part> under the sun can juggle, ski and bake, but its <part>heart</part> just isn't in it. It rolls its eyes, sighs loudly and lets the eggs drop on the floor. What a terrible <kanji>attitude</kanji>.
態.on: To look a bit more serious it puts on a <sound>tie</sound>, then chews the end of it.
態.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' wails the cook as it hurls an egg across the ba<sound>za</sound>ar and splats a <sound>to</sound>tem pole: on purpose.

系.meaning: Grandma keeps one long <part>thread</part> that runs from her sewing box through every family photo on the wall, an ancestor knotted on at each one. Each new baby gets a little red <part>slash</part> of ink where it ties on. Follow it back and you see the whole <kanji>lineage</kanji>.
系.on: At every birthday a fresh knot is tied around the candles of the <sound>ca</sound>ke.

統.meaning: A weaver gathers <part>thread</part> from every village in the land and uses it to <part>fill</part> one enormous carpet, stitching all their patterns into a single design. Step back far enough and you see the whole kingdom at once: the <kanji>overall</kanji> picture.
統.on: Right in the middle she sews the king's big <sound>toe</sound>, poking out of his slipper.
統.kun: The king rules from the centre of the carpet, eating <sound>su</sound>shi off its pattern.

因.meaning: Something <part>large</part> is stuck in the <part>cage</part> in the kitchen, rattling the bars. Smashed plates, flour everywhere, the dog hiding: what started it all? The bars bend, and out climbs Grandpa, who went in after a cookie. He's the <kanji>cause</kanji>.
因.on: He leaves an <sound>in</sound>k footprint on every tile on his way out.
因.kun: It all began when his <sound>yo</sound>gurt pot rolled in there first.

敗.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> enters a sailing race with a paper <part>fan</part> as its only sail. It flaps and flaps, the boats zoom past, and then a seagull snatches the fan away. The shellfish sinks gently to the bottom: total <kanji>failure</kanji>.
敗.on: The seagull carries the fan off to a <sound>hi</sound>ve on the cliff, and the bees use it to cool their honey.
敗.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>! <sound>Boo</sound>!' jeer the crabs as the beaten shellfish crawls home.

掛.meaning: A tidy sailor has no cupboard, so he drives his <part>anchor</part> into a <part>double mound</part> of mud and uses its hooks as a rack. On go his hat, his boots, even a leaky <part>faucet</part> he found on the beach. He loves to <kanji>hang</kanji> things.
掛.on: Last of all he ties on the string of his <sound>ki</sound>te, which flutters above the mound all night.
掛.kun: Then a wet <sound>ca</sound>rp, hooked up by its tail to dry in the wind.

背.meaning: Two grumpy explorers at the <part>north</part> pole have had a row, so they sit back to back on a sledge under the <part>moon</part>, propping each other up. Neither will turn round all night. By dawn each knows every bump of the other's <kanji>back</kanji>.
背.on: A frozen <sound>hi</sound>ve sits wedged between their spines, humming and keeping them warm.
背.kun: A red <sound>se</sound>tter curls up and sleeps across their shoulders.

景.meaning: The <part>capital</part> charges ten coins to climb its tallest tower and watch the <part>sun</part> go down. At the top you find a single bench facing a brick wall, with a sunset painted on it. Still, everyone agrees it's lovely <kanji>scenery</kanji>.
景.on: Beside the bench, a man sells slices of <sound>ca</sound>ke shaped like little sunsets.

攻.meaning: A carpenter is quietly sanding at his <part>workbench</part> when a folding <part>fan</part> leaps off the shelf and slaps him on the head, again and again. He swings a plank; it dodges and slaps again. That fan is full of <kanji>aggression</kanji>.
攻.on: He fights back by jamming an ice-cream <sound>co</sound>ne onto its tip.
攻.kun: His red <sound>se</sound>tter joins the attack, lobbing a <sound>me</sound>lon at the fan.

勤.meaning: Every dawn an old farmer flexes his <part>muscle</part> and lifts the same <part>wheat sheaf</part> over his head a hundred times, then puts it down exactly where it was. Rain or snow, he never misses a morning. The whole village admires his <kanji>diligence</kanji>.
勤.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher on the fence counts the lifts out loud for him.
勤.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes at the dust, then leans the sheaf against a <sound>to</sound>tem pole and goes off to work.

映.meaning: A pond in the <part>center</part> of the park is so still that the <part>sun</part> stops overhead every noon to check its rays in it, like a mirror. The pond hands back every sparkle. It loves to <kanji>reflect</kanji>.
映.on: Then an <sound>a</sound>corn drops in with a plop, and the sun's face wobbles.
映.kun: A duck drops a noodle of <sound>u</sound>don on the sun's face and sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

欲.meaning: A giant lying in a <part>valley</part> gives a huge <part>yawn</part> and just keeps his mouth open: rivers, sheep and a whole bakery slide in. Still hungry, he gazes over at the next valley with a deep <kanji>longing</kanji>.
欲.on: What he dreams of most is a single egg <sound>yolk</sound> the size of a lake.
欲.kun: Or a <sound>hot</sound>dog as long as the valley, with that yolk on top. He wants it so much.

玉.meaning: The <part>king</part> sneezes, and a single shiny <part>dot</part> flies off his nose and lands at his feet. The court gasps, polishes it and sets it on a velvet cushion, where it sparkles. Now it's the kingdom's most famous <kanji>jewel</kanji>.
玉.on: The court chef swears it's only a bi<sound>g</sound> <sound>yolk</sound>, boiled hard and shiny.
玉.kun: The king hides it in a <sound>ta</sound>co shell, but his <sound>Ma</sound> finds it and wears it as a ring.
